newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Rwandan refugees in Tanzania told to go home.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan refugees in Tanzania told to go home.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency and the Tanzanian government told more than half a million Rwandan refugees in Tanzania on Thursday to go home by the end of this month, a U.N. official said.

"Today there has been a message by both the government and UNHCR -- a joint message from the government and us -- that the refugees are wanted to leave by the end of December," said Lennart Kotsalainen, deputy head of the office of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).
"We are putting out the message that it is time for these people to go back. Hopefully by the end of this evening they will get the message," he told Reuters in the Tanzanian capital.

"Obviously some will be very hesitant but once the ball starts rolling probably it will be a mass return," Kotsalainen added. He said radio broadcasts were being made to inform the refugees of the order.
UNHCR and Tanzanian officials have sought a mass return from Tanzania since an estimated 600,000 Rwandan refugees trekked home from camps in eastern Zaire between November 15 and 19.
A total of 542,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees fled to eastern Tanzania in 1994 during civil war and the genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates by Hutu troops, militiamen and mobs.
The Tanzanian government has demanded all Rwandan refugees leave by the end of the year but has assured UNHCR it will not use force to expel civilians from its territory.

Some aid workers have warned that triggering the desired exodus from Tanzania will be difficult and note refugees left eastern Zaire only because fighting forced them from their camps near the Rwandan border.
Many Hutu refugees in Tanzania, like those previously in Zaire, said they feared going home because they might be jailed or attacked in reprisal for the genocide, which some took part in.
Aid workers say Hutu extremist militiamen and former Rwandan troops who have ordered refugees not to return must be separated before innocent refugees can be expected to leave.
UNHCR sources told Reuters the Tanzanian government had a list of 200 intimidators who might be separated from the main body of refugees prior to the repatriation deadline.

"We think there's a good opportunity now the refugees will respond to the messages by the government and UNHCR," said Kotsalainen, adding the government had promised not to use force against "normal refugees."
In a joint statement on Thursday, the Tanzanian government and UNHCR said Rwandan authorities had given assurances they would receive all refugees from the Tanzania camps.
"On the basis of these undertakings, the Government of the United Republic of Tanzania has decided that all Rwandese refugees in Tanzania are expected to return home by 31 December, 1996."
"The Tanzanian government and UNHCR, therefore urges that all refugees make preparations to return before that date."

It said the Home Affairs (Interior) Ministry would be responsible for the repatriation, in cooperation with UNHCR. Police would protect refugees and would be supported, if necessary, by Tanzanian troops.
Kotsalainen said UNHCR would provide transport across the border.
